description: baseline: lora_train_generative.py as-is (--lean-prompt --df-path emnllp-dialog-flow-dialog-flow.json, batch-size=1, defaults: epochs=3 lora_r=8 q_proj,v_proj lr=2e-4 grad-accum=4), best at epoch 1/3 (mean_macro_f1 then DROPS to 0.659 ep2, 0.584 ep3 -- overfitting/instability after ep1). ~33-37min/epoch (batch=1 + sequential generate() dev eval is the bottleneck), ~103min total

exp1a: baseline + batch-size 1->8, grad-accum 4->1 (same effective batch=4, hoping to parallelize the slow batch=1 generate() eval). CRASHED epoch1 step0: CUDA OOM in logits.float() inside HF's ForCausalLMLoss -- that upcast scales batch*seq_len*vocab_size regardless of loss masking, and with max_length=4096 + a long outlier in the batch it needed 15.57GiB alone. Token-length check: fixed prompt scaffolding (lean+df) is 1338 tok, segment text p50=1182 p90=2476 p99=4092 -- most examples are well under 4096 but the tail is long enough that batch=8 padding to a worst-case member blows up. Retrying with a smaller batch bump (2) instead of 8

exp1b: baseline + batch-size 1->2, grad-accum 4->2 (effective batch held at 4, same optimizer step count 589/epoch), expandable_segments:True for OOM headroom. WORSE on both axes: mean_macro_f1 0.724->0.563 at ep1 (st3 cratered 0.602->0.253), AND slower (64-68min/epoch vs baseline's 33-37min) -- pairing random-length examples into batches of 2 pads to the longer member, adding real compute waste, and the different minibatch composition changed the (noisy, only 589 steps/epoch) optimization trajectory for the worse. Reverting to batch-size=1/grad-accum=4

exp2: baseline recipe (batch-size=1, grad-accum=4) unchanged, but added+used --eval-batch-size=16 (new flag, decouples dev generate() batching from train batch -- eval-time generate() has no logits.float()-over-full-vocab blowup like training does, so it's safe to batch much larger) + epochs capped to 1 (baseline+exp1b both peaked at ep1 and degraded after). Epoch time 32.7min->26.2min (train ~22min unchanged, eval 10-11min->4.2min). mean_macro_f1=0.658 vs baseline's identical-recipe ep1=0.724 -- pure run-to-run noise (same seed, same hyperparams, only eval batching differs, which shouldn't affect greedy-decode correctness), not attributable to the eval-batch-size change. Adopting eval-batch-size=16 + epochs=1 as new standing default for this track

exp3: exp2 recipe + target-modules q_proj,v_proj->q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj (full attn+FFN LoRA coverage, mirrors the roberta track's biggest win). trainable params 1.15M->5.05M (0.19%->0.84%). mean_macro_f1 0.658->0.745 (using exp2's identical-recipe run as the fair baseline since same seed/hyperparams otherwise), st3 0.447->0.630 and st3_family 0.624->0.793 driving most of it -- same pattern as roberta's FFN win landing hardest on the weakest subtask. Cost: train phase 22min->31min (more modules in the compute graph), eval unchanged ~5min. Adopting full target-modules as new standing default

exp4: exp3 recipe + lora_r 8->16, lora_alpha 16->32 (same alpha/r=2 ratio, doubled capacity on top of full attn+FFN coverage). mean_macro_f1 0.745->0.566, well beyond the ~0.09 noise band seen between identical-recipe runs (exp2 baseline-repeat) -- more capacity destabilizes/overfits this single-epoch, 2353-example generative SFT rather than helping. Reverting to lora_r=8

exp5: exp3 recipe (r=8, full target-modules) + lr 2e-4->1e-4. mean_macro_f1 0.745->0.706, within the ~0.09 noise band established by exp2 (st3/st3_family actually held up fine at 0.616/0.841, st1 dropped 0.811->0.637 driving the delta). Not a clear win, reverting to lr=2e-4. Noise is substantial enough here that small (~0.04-0.09) deltas aren't reliably attributable to a single-run change -- looking for bigger-effect-size levers going forward

exp6: exp3 recipe + grad-accum-steps 4->8 (effective batch 4->8, steadier updates, same per-step batch=1 so no OOM/composition risk). Killed by user before completion (both the initial run, lost to a session restart mid-load, and the restart, killed directly) -- no result, not yet retried
